title: Developer adapter conformance and sample harness
author: Priya Shah
body:
Overview:

This page defines the conformance levels, automated checks, and a lightweight sample harness for third-party developer adapters that integrate with Redwood Inference SDKs and runtime. The goal is to provide a short, reproducible on-ramp for adapter authors, a minimal CI gate focused on safety and telemetry compatibility, and a troubleshooting runbook for the most common integration failures.

Why this exists:
- Multiple internal and partner-built adapters (language-specific adapters, cloud connectors, and on-prem proxy layers) must present a consistent surface to SDKs and telemetry collectors.
- Inconsistent adapters are the leading cause of support churn: mis-attributed latency, missing error codes, and telemetry schema drift.
- A small, automated conformance harness reduces review time and provides a reproducible developer experience for adapter authors.

Audience:
- SDK authors and adapter maintainers
- Solutions engineers working on partner integrations
- Developer advocates and QA engineers responsible for releasing adapter packages

Conformance levels (summary):
1) Bronze — Basic API compatibility and buildable examples. Required for early-stage community adapters.
2) Silver — Must pass the sample harness smoke tests, emit base telemetry fields, and include a README with integration steps. Required for self-serve adapters in the docs site.
3) Gold — Full conformance: CI-enabled test run, telemetry schema validation, retry and backoff policy tests, and documented SLOs. Required for any adapter promoted to official Redwood distribution.

Required criteria by level (short checklist):
- Bronze:
  - Exposes adapter factory or registration function compatible with SDK loader API.
  - Includes minimal example that runs a single generation call.
  - Build/package instructions included.
- Silver:
  - All Bronze items.
  - Passes the sample harness smoke tests (see Quickstart below).
  - Emits telemetry events with the required base fields (adapter_id, sdk_version, request_id, duration_ms).
  - Contains a short trouble-shooting section in README.
- Gold:
  - All Silver items.
  - CI job that runs harness in headless mode and uploads results to the internal test-results bucket.
  - Implements at least one configurable fallback (local stub or alternative endpoint).
  - Documents expected latency SLO (p50/p95) for the adapter under a short synthetic workload.

Smoke test matrix (table):
- Represented below as an ASCII table for easy copy/paste into CI job docs.

| Test name                     | Purpose                                         | Failure indicator                   | Retryable |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|-----------|
| basic-generation-step        | Verifies adapter can execute a single generate() | non-zero exit or missing response   | no        |
| streaming-handshake          | Verifies streaming handoff and resume semantics  | truncated stream or out-of-order    | yes       |
| error-propagation            | Ensures the adapter surfaces upstream errors     | swallowed error or 500 -> 200       | no        |
| telemetry-schema             | Validate required telemetry fields and types     | missing fields or incorrect type    | no        |
| retry-backoff-behaviour     | Confirm backoff used when endpoint returns 429   | no exponential backoff observed     | yes       |

Quickstart: run the sample harness locally

Prerequisites:
- Python 3.10+ or Node 18+ depending on adapter language
- Docker (optional for running the fake-runtime server)
- Git checkout of adapter repository

Steps:
1) Clone the adapter repo and change into the example folder:
   - git clone git@github.com:redwood-inference/thirdparty-adapter-example.git
   - cd thirdparty-adapter-example/examples/minimal
2) Ensure the adapter exposes the test entrypoint (typical file: tests/harness_entry.py or tests/harness_entry.js)
3) Start the fake runtime server (this simulates Redwood runtime behavior):
   - docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 redwood/fake-runtime:latest
4) Run the harness script: (Python example):
   - python -m adapter_harness.run --server http://localhost:8080 --adapter ./dist/adapter_pkg

Expected output:
- A short report in the console: PASS/FAIL for each smoke test and a JSON artifact written to ./harness-results/result-summary.json.

CI integration snippet (GitHub Actions)
- Example YAML (copy/paste into .github/workflows/harness.yml):

  name: Adapter harness smoke tests
  on: [push, pull_request]
  jobs:
    harness:
      runs-on: ubuntu-latest
      steps:
        - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        - name: Set up Python
          uses: actions/setup-python@v4
          with:
            python-version: '3.10'
        - name: Build adapter
          run: ./scripts/build_adapter.sh
        - name: Start fake runtime
          run: docker run -d -p 8080:8080 redwood/fake-runtime:latest
        - name: Run harness
          run: python -m adapter_harness.run --server http://localhost:8080 --adapter ./dist/adapter_pkg --output ./harness-results
        - name: Upload results
          uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
          with:
            name: harness-results
            path: ./harness-results

Telemetry contract (required base fields)
- All adapters at Silver level and above MUST emit telemetry events that include at least the following keys (JSON event envelope):
  - event_type: string (examples: request.start, request.finish, error.occurred)
  - adapter_id: string (unique short name for the adapter, e.g., 'py-http-adapter-v1')
  - sdk_version: string (semver for the SDK integration)
  - request_id: string (opaque id propagated from SDK to adapter)
  - duration_ms: number (total time spent in adapter for the request)
  - status_code: number (HTTP or adapter-native code if applicable)
  - sampling_rate: number (0.0-1.0) optional but recommended

Example event (JSON):
{
  "event_type": "request.finish",
  "adapter_id": "py-http-adapter-v1",
  "sdk_version": "1.4.2",
  "request_id": "r-8b74a2",
  "duration_ms": 145.2,
  "status_code": 200
}

Adapter SDK interface (summary)
- The adapter should implement a minimal interface that the Redwood SDK loader understands. This sample interface is intentionally small to support many languages:

- Python (pseudo-signature):
  - class Adapter:
    - def __init__(self, config: dict) -> None:
    - def handle_request(self, request: dict) -> dict:
    - def shutdown(self) -> None:

- Node (pseudo-signature):
  - module.exports = class Adapter {
    - constructor(config) { }
    - async handleRequest(request) { }
    - async shutdown() { }
  }

Error handling guidelines:
- Surface upstream errors with clear type and message. Do not translate all errors to a generic 500. Use the following mapping table when possible:
  - Adapter timeout -> 504 (with detailed timeout_ms field)
  - Upstream 429 -> 429 (include retry-after if provided)
  - Validation error -> 400

Deployment and SLO documentation (recommended for Gold level):
- Provide a short table documenting expected latency under a small synthetic load:

| Load profile    | p50 latency (ms) | p95 latency (ms) | notes                         |
|-----------------|------------------|------------------|-------------------------------|
| single-threaded | 40               | 95               | local dev with Docker         |
| 4 parallel reqs | 55               | 210              | containerized, 2 vCPU test VM |

Release checklist for adapter maintainers:
1) Ensure README includes integration snippet and telemetry requirements.
2) Run harness locally and attach result JSON to PR.
3) Add the harness job to CI for silver/gold classification.
4) If Gold, add runbook and expected SLO table to the docs folder.
5) Assign an on-call owner in CODEOWNERS and mention in PR.

Owner and escalation
- Primary owner: adapter package maintainer listed in CODEOWNERS.
- Secondary owner: SDK team (eng-developer-experience).
- Escalation flow:
  1) Open a support ticket in Zendesk with the harness-results artifact and telemetry sample.
  2) If critical (customer incident), page SDK on-call (see /confluence/eng-oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems for on-call roster).

Common failures and troubleshooting (runbook excerpts):
- Failure: harness reports "telemetry-schema" failure
  - Symptom: missing adapter_id or request_id in event sample
  - Quick fix: ensure telemetry emitter attaches SDK-provided context object. Example change (Node):
    - emitter.emit('request.finish', Object.assign({}, sdkContext, { duration_ms }))
- Failure: streaming-handshake truncated
  - Symptom: consumers report partial outputs, harness shows non-terminating stream
  - Quick fix: verify your adapter flushes buffer on newline and supports the resume token header. See streaming-handshake test description in harness README.
- Failure: retry-backoff-behaviour fails in CI
  - Symptom: harness shows constant retry intervals (no backoff)
  - Quick fix: adopt our small backoff helper in utils/backoff.{js,py} (exponential with jitter).

Sample artifacts produced by harness:
- ./harness-results/result-summary.json (per-test PASS/FAIL with timestamps)
- ./harness-results/events-sample.json (telemetry event samples captured during tests)
- ./harness-results/metrics.csv (simple CSV of durations)

Security and data handling notes:
- Never include full customer prompts in telemetry events. Telemetry must send only metadata and safe hashes for debugging. The harness strips prompt text by default; adapters must honor the leave-text-out configuration when present.

Related pages and references:
- SDK loader API (internal link): /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples/sdk-loader-api-reference-2024
- Telemetry schema definition: /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/telemetry-schema-v2

Change log:
- 2024-11-12: Document created (initial Bronze/Silver/Gold model and harness quickstart).
- 2025-02-10: Added CI integration snippet, updated telemetry contract to require sdk_version and sampling_rate recommendation.

If you are an adapter author and want the official fake-runtime image or CI template, contact eng-developer-experience@redwood.ai and include the repository link and preferred language runtime.
